problem: Behavior cloning on human ObjectNav demonstrations (Habitat-Web) generalizes poorly to states it never saw and is expensive to scale: 77k demos cost about 2378 annotation hours. RL from scratch with sparse reward barely learns, and RL with dense rewards needs careful reward engineering. Naively finetuning a BC policy with actor-critic RL fails, because BC gives no critic and the randomly initialized critic causes destructive early updates.
motivation: RL is trivially scalable once annotated 3D scans exist, while human demonstrations encode useful ObjectNav-specific search behavior. BC-pretraining could therefore bootstrap RL and even make sparse-success rewards workable. It is also unclear whether cheap automatically generated demonstrations (shortest paths, frontier exploration) could replace human ones, and how BC→RL gains scale with demonstration count.
key_idea: The policy is pretrained with behavior cloning on human demonstrations and then finetuned with DD-PPO using a sparse success reward. Finetuning runs in two phases: first only the critic is learned on rollouts from the frozen BC policy, then the actor learning rate is warmed up while the critic learning rate is decayed, which avoids the destructive updates from an untrained critic.
insight: The main obstacle in BC→RL is the uninitialized critic, not the reward. On HM3D val (20k HD pretraining, BC 52.0 SR): naive BC→RL-FT reaches only 53.6 SR; adding a critic-only phase gives 56.7; adding critic LR decay gives 59.4, or 58.2 with actor warmup instead; the full schedule gives 61.9, beating VPT-style KL-regularized finetuning (59.7). Demonstration source matters beyond BC accuracy. With checkpoints matched at ~48% BC train success, RL-FT from human demos reaches 66.1 val SR versus 51.3 for frontier exploration and 43.6 for shortest paths; shortest paths overfit and frontier exploration underfits. RL gains shrink as BC data grows: +10.1 at 20k demos and +6.3 at 77k. 35k demos reach 66.4 versus 70.4 at 77k, and frontier-exploration BC saturates at ~70k demos.
method: Human demonstration collection: 77k ObjectNav teleoperation demos on HM3D-Semantics v0.1 via the Habitat-WebGL/MTurk infrastructure (~2378 hours).

Policy architecture: ResNet50 RGB encoder (DINO-pretrained on Omnidata, i.e. the OVRL recipe, finetuned during training); GPS+Compass and one-hot goal embedded with FC layers to 32-d; concatenated features go into a 2-layer 2048-d GRU that outputs discrete actions. Color-jitter and random-shift augmentation; depth is not used.
BC pretraining: cross-entropy imitation with inflection weighting (upweights timesteps where the action changes); distributed BC for 500M steps on 64 GPUs, Adam at lr 1e-3 with linear decay.
Phase 1, critic learning: actor, CNN and shared weights frozen; critic final layer initialized near zero; critic trained for ~8M steps on rollouts sampled (not argmax) from the frozen BC policy.

Phase 2, interactive learning: actor RNN unfrozen while the CNN and non-visual embeddings stay frozen. Between 8M and 12M steps the critic lr decays from 2.5e-4 to 1.5e-5 while the actor lr warms up from 0 to 1.5e-5; both then stay at 1.5e-5. Shared params use the lower lr.
RL finetuning: DD-PPO with GAE (γ=0.99, τ=0.95), sparse success-only reward, 300M steps on 16 GPUs.

Demonstration-source study: BC and BC→RL compared across shortest-path (240k), frontier-exploration (70k, scaled 10k–150k) and human (77k, scaled 2k–77k) demos. Includes an equal-BC-train-success control and adversarial SP-/FE-favoring val subsplits.

setting.backbone: ResNet50 (DINO/OVRL-pretrained on Omnidata, finetuned) + 2-layer 2048-d GRU policy, trained with BC then DD-PPO
setting.training_data: 77k human ObjectNav demonstrations on HM3D-Semantics v0.1 train scenes (~2378 annotation hours) for BC (500M steps), then 300M steps of on-policy RL with sparse success reward in HM3D train scenes. Analysis also uses 240k shortest-path demos and 10k–150k frontier-exploration demos.

numbers_note: Some own results appear only in figures: Fig. 1 (BC vs BC→RL scaling over 2k–77k human demos), Fig. 4 (BC→RL from SP/FE/HD) and Fig. 6 (FE scaling). The text quotes some numbers from these figures: with ~48% BC train success controlled, val RL-FT SR is HD 66.1 / FE 51.3 / SP 43.6. On adversarial val subsets (Table 5), RL-FT from HD reaches 57.2 SR on both the SP-favoring and FE-favoring subsets; RL-FT from SP/FE reaches 34.8/43.0. BC-only with SP (240k) scores 6.4 SR / 5.0 SPL and FE (70k) 44.9 / 21.5 on val. The test-standard and test-challenge splits are both mapped to 'test' and distinguished in 'extra'.
results: PIRLNav reaches 65.0% SR / 33.0% SPL on both HM3D test-standard and test-challenge (Habitat ObjectNav Challenge 2022), and 70.4 SR / 34.1 SPL on val. It beats the previous best published method, Stretch (60.0/34.0 test-std; 56.0/29.0 test-challenge), by +5.0 SR on test-standard, with SPL 1 point worse there and 4 points better on test-challenge. It also beats ProcTHOR-Large (54/32) and Habitat-Web (55/22). With 20k demos, its two-phase finetuning gets 61.9 SR versus 59.7 for VPT-style KL-regularized finetuning and 53.6 for naive BC→RL.
limitations: Still depends on expensive human teleoperation demos (77k, ~2378 h); RL gains diminish as BC data grows, and cheap frontier-exploration demos saturate at ~70k and underperform.

Failure analysis of 592 val failures: 27% missing annotations and 9% navmesh issues, plus 21% inter-floor (stairs) failures, 20% recognition failures, 11–12% last-mile navigation and 5% semantic confusion.

Compute-heavy (500M BC steps on 64 GPUs + 300M RL steps on 16 GPUs). Off-policy or demo-replay methods such as DAPG were not feasible at this scale, so the method is limited to on-policy PPO finetuning.
